question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

options.A: Managing hospital admissions during disease outbreaks
options.B: Eliminating the need for community health clinics
options.C: Enabling people to increase control over their health
options.D: Focusing solely on the treatment of chronic illnesses

explanation: Health promotion aims to empower individuals and communities to take charge of their own well-being rather than just treating them when they fall ill. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease prevention?

options.A: Disease prevention ignores clinical guidelines completely
options.B: Disease prevention focuses on building overall lifestyle resilience
options.C: Health promotion addresses broader social and environmental factors
options.D: Health promotion relies only on pharmaceutical interventions

explanation: While disease prevention targets specific illnesses, health promotion takes a wider view to foster complete physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is multi-sectoral action necessary in health promotion?

options.A: Health depends on factors beyond just medical care
options.B: Funding is only available through agriculture ministries
options.C: Communities refuse to listen to nurses alone
options.D: Doctors cannot work without government supervision

explanation: Factors like education, housing, and food security heavily influence health, requiring cooperation across different sectors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: What does the principle of equity mean for healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: Fair distribution of resources to reduce urban and rural disparities
options.B: Building primary health centers only in state capitals
options.C: Providing the exact same medication to every single patient
options.D: Ensuring that wealthy patients pay for poorer hospital wings

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness, ensuring that underserved rural areas receive adequate attention and health resources compared to cities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: In which year was the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion established?
explanation: The Ottawa Charter was adopted at the first International Conference on Health Promotion held in Canada in 1986. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: What was a major shift promoted by the Ottawa Charter?

options.A: Replacing traditional medicine with foreign pharmaceuticals completely
options.B: Focusing exclusively on urban sanitation projects
options.C: Handing over all hospital management to international donors
options.D: Moving away from purely curative hospital care toward prevention

explanation: The charter emphasized community action and preventive health services rather than just treating sick patients in hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations is an example of which level of prevention?
explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts by protecting healthy individuals through vaccination and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening at a local market. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: Screenings catch asymptomatic conditions early, allowing for prompt treatment which is the hallmark of secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: What do social determinants of health refer to?

options.A: The genetic mutations passed down through family lineages
options.B: The specific protocols used by doctors inside operating theaters
options.C: The conditions in which people are born, grow, live, and work
options.D: The pricing structures of pharmaceutical drugs in pharmacies

explanation: Social determinants encompass everyday living and working conditions that heavily influence physical and mental health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses consider female literacy when planning health programs?

options.A: Uneducated women refuse to visit primary healthcare centers
options.B: Government grants are only given to literate female patients
options.C: Educated mothers are better equipped to manage family health and nutrition
options.D: Hospitals require literate women to fill out administrative admission forms

explanation: Women often act as primary caregivers; improving their education directly improves child health, hygiene, and nutritional practices at home. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which health promotion approach focuses mainly on providing facts to encourage informed personal choices?
explanation: The educational approach supplies knowledge and information so individuals can voluntarily change unhealthy behaviors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of the empowerment approach in community health?

options.A: Helping people gain the skills to change their own living conditions
options.B: Forcing local leaders to build hospitals without community input
options.C: Training every citizen to become a licensed professional nurse
options.D: Handing out financial loans to open private medical clinics

explanation: Empowerment builds self-reliance, enabling communities to take charge of local health challenges rather than relying solely on outsiders. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is involving traditional and religious leaders important in Nigerian community health?

options.A: They are legally required to sign all hospital discharge papers
options.B: They provide the financial budget for primary health centers
options.C: They act as certified medical doctors during emergencies
options.D: They hold significant influence and help build local trust

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders command deep respect, making their endorsement crucial for community acceptance of health initiatives. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: What happens when a health project lacks community ownership?

options.A: The government automatically takes over maintenance costs
options.B: It often collapses once external funding and support are withdrawn
options.C: The community builds a better facility on their own
options.D: Local health workers receive higher salaries from donors

explanation: Without local buy-in and ownership, projects fail to sustain themselves once initial donor involvement ends. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: When a nurse lobbies local authorities for better waste disposal, which role is being performed?
explanation: An advocate speaks up for the community's health needs, influencing policy makers and local leaders to improve environmental conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: A nurse organizes a town hall meeting for villagers to discuss rising malaria cases. Which nursing function does this represent?
explanation: Acting as a facilitator involves bringing people together to communicate, organize, and solve shared health problems collectively. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge for health program evaluation in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive surplus of reliable digital data systems
options.B: Difficulty in measuring long-term behavioral changes
options.C: Poor data collection at primary health centers
options.D: Short project funding timelines from donors

explanation: Nigeria struggles with weak data collection systems rather than having an excess of reliable digital infrastructure. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: Why is evaluating health promotion harder than evaluating a simple surgical procedure?

options.A: Surgeries do not require any post-operative hospital records
options.B: Patients always tell the exact truth during health surveys
options.C: Long-term behavioral and lifestyle changes are difficult to measure
options.D: Health promotion programs never involve any measurable goals

explanation: Unlike a direct surgical outcome, changes in community health habits take years to materialize and are hard to track accurately. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)
